Subject: Blended annual commit offer & onboarding timeline

Hi Claire —

Thanks for taking the time on our call earlier. Per our discussion, I attached a short blended-commit proposal that gives Starter / Growth / Enterprise token bands plus a recommended onboarding timeline. High level highlights:

- Starter: 10M tokens/year — suitable for feature-level rollout and pilot teams.
- Growth: 100M tokens/year — targeted for product-wide usage and mid-stage scaling.
- Enterprise: 1B tokens/year — for full-platform adoption and heavy production workloads.

Each tier includes a suggested per-token price, basic SLAs, and recommended ramp windows. The attachment is a concise one-pager with pricing bands and onboarding milestones: 2-week integration, 4-week validation, then prod ramp.

Please review and share your expected 12-month usage profile (rough monthly cadence is fine). If you can confirm an expected commit tier, I’ll scope a PO path and draft the SLA amendment for legal.

I’m available M–F and you can grab 30 minutes on my calendar here: https://cal.com/sean-gallagher/30min

Best,

1) Can committed tokens be carried forward across quarters or year-end?

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Clarifications from PilotData on commits & SLAs — need pricing/legal language

Team — forwarding Claire’s questions below. Quick thoughts, please:

- Carryover: Standard approach we discussed in Q1 playbook — allow up to 25% annual carryover, any remainder expires. For Starter we should probably keep carryover to 0–10% to prevent stockpiling.
- Overage: Recommend staged overage pricing: list price for first 10% over, then 50% of list thereafter up to 50% overage; Enterprise can have a capped overage rate at a negotiated blended price.
- SLA: Draft SLA amendment should include p50 latency target (50ms token gen on hosted API under baseline) and p95 target (250ms) for Growth/Enterprise. Starter should have best-effort latency and 99.5% availability; Growth/Enterprise 99.9% with credits.
- Dedicated lead time: say 6–8 weeks for Growth (bumped up by GPU availability), 10–12 weeks for Enterprise (reserved pools). Match with capacity ops.

Ask: Priyom — can you run margin on proposed per-token numbers below and confirm whether the discounts leave room for promotion credit? Karthik — can you draft a short SLA amendment we can attach? I’ll incorporate and send a clear written offer back to Claire/Purchasing.

Subject: Updated offer: blended commit tiers, overage rules, and onboarding roadmap

Hi Claire / Procurement team —

Appreciate the quick follow-up. Based on your forecast and internal alignment, here’s a written offer you can take to purchasing. The attached PDF is the same content below in a clean format for your review.

Summary (annual committed tokens / per-token price / discount vs list):
- Starter: 10,000,000 tokens/year — $0.00090 / token (approx. 10% off list) — no guaranteed dedicated capacity; best-effort latency; limited 10% annual carryover.
- Growth: 100,000,000 tokens/year — $0.00075 / token (approx. 25% off list) — 99.9% availability SLA with credits; p50 50ms / p95 250ms guidance; Dedicated capacity lead time: 6–8 weeks. 25% annual carryover.
- Enterprise: 1,000,000,000 tokens/year — $0.00055 / token (approx. 45% off list) — 99.95% availability SLA with higher credits; dedicated reserved pools; lead time 10–12 weeks; 25% carryover + negotiated capped overage rate.

Overage rules: first 10% overage billed at list price; 10–50% overage billed at 75% of list; above 50% by exception and subject to re-negotiation. For Enterprise customers we can offer a blended overage rate cap as part of the contract.

Payment & PO path: Net 30 preferred; early-pay discount options (1.5% for Net 10). We can provide an MSA amendment and a short SOW for onboarding milestones.

Onboarding roadmap (typical):
- Week 0–2: Kickoff & integration — API keys, test environment, basic prompts.
- Week 2–6: Validation & perf testing — load tests, KV caching config, model profile tuning.
- Week 6–10: Pilot to prod ramp — can be longer if Dedicated lead time applies.

Next steps for you:
1) Confirm preferred commit tier and whether you want Dedicated reserved pools for Growth/Enterprise.
2) If yes, we’ll issue the Final Offer PDF and SLA draft for procurement review.
3) Provide PO/PO request or let us know if you want a short redline window (legal usually requests 5 business days).

Attachments: [attachment: Final-offer-20270524.pdf (PDF, 480KB)], [attachment: SLA-Amendment-draft.docx (DOCX, 36KB)]

If helpful, I can carve out 30 minutes later this week to walk procurement through the numbers — grabbing time on my calendar is here: https://cal.com/sean-gallagher/30min

Thanks and speak soon,
